title: Gateway: add metrics for streaming disconnect reasons + tool-call parse errors
author: Allison Grant
release_notes: Added gateway metrics for streaming disconnect reasons and tool-call argument parse errors; introduced a troubleshooting dashboard and alerts to detect regressions and proxy-related disconnects.
body:
Title: Gateway: add metrics for streaming disconnect reasons + tool-call parse errors

Context
Support and DevEx are seeing a recurring set of issues that are hard to triage with current telemetry: (1) streaming disconnects (often behind proxies / LB idle timeouts), and (2) tool-call argument parsing failures caused by partial JSON deltas (esp. parallel tool calls). This PR adds low-cardinality metrics in the gateway to attribute disconnects and to quantify tool-call parse errors, and wires them into a small dashboard + alert thresholds.

What’s in this PR
- New Prometheus counters for streaming disconnects with a bounded reason taxonomy:
  - redwood_gateway_stream_disconnect_total{reason, route, customer_tier}
  - redwood_gateway_stream_disconnect_bytes_total{reason, route} (optional, helps detect proxy buffering / truncation patterns)
  - redwood_gateway_stream_active{route} (gauge)
- New counters for tool-call argument parsing issues:
  - redwood_gateway_tool_call_parse_error_total{stage, parser, route}
    - stage: delta | final
    - parser: json | schema (schema = structured-output validation step when tool args are expected to conform)
  - redwood_gateway_tool_call_incomplete_args_total{route} (incremented when stream ends before a tool call’s args are complete)
- Conservative labeling: no customer_id/model_id; route is normalized, tier is coarse (free|pro|enterprise), and reason/stage/parser are enums.
- Reason taxonomy used for disconnects (documented inline and in the dashboard description):
  - client_cancel: client closed connection / explicit cancellation
  - idle_timeout: gateway idle timeout hit (no downstream flush)
  - upstream_timeout: upstream request timed out (runtime/backend)
  - upstream_closed: upstream ended stream unexpectedly
  - proxy_error: common proxy/LB failure modes (e.g. broken pipe, connection reset)
  - internal_error: gateway error while writing SSE/chunked response
  - unknown: fallback bucket
- Grafana dashboard (internal): https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/streaming-tools-triage/gateway-streaming-tools-triage
  - Panels: disconnect rate by reason, time series of parse errors, top routes, and correlation view (disconnects vs parse errors).
- Alert thresholds (PrometheusRule):
  - StreamingDisconnectRateHigh: >0.75% of streaming requests disconnect with non-client_cancel reasons over 10m (min 2k req/10m)
  - ToolCallParseErrorsSpike: parse errors > 25/min over 5m on any route (min 500 tool-call events/5m)
  - ToolArgsIncompleteRateHigh: incomplete args >0.5% over 10m on tool-enabled routes

Implementation notes
- Disconnect reason mapping is based on the existing error surfaces from the SSE/chunked writer + upstream client; the new code threads a typed termination cause through the stream lifecycle so we don’t guess from stringly errors.
- Tool-call parse errors are counted in two places:
  1) delta aggregation step (partial JSON chunks fail incremental parsing / concatenation)
  2) finalization step (final parse/validation fails after stream ends)
- All error counters intentionally exclude payload content; we only record stage/parser/route.
- Tests cover: reason mapping for common net/http errors, ensuring labels don’t explode, and a regression test for “stream ends mid tool args” counting incomplete args.

Files / areas touched (high level)
- gateway/streaming/sse_writer.go: add typed termination reason + instrumentation hooks
- gateway/streaming/disconnect_reasons.go: normalization/mapping of error causes
- gateway/tools/args_aggregator.go: counters for parse_error + incomplete_args
- gateway/metrics/registry.go: new metric definitions
- deploy/monitoring/prometheus_rules/gateway_streaming_tools.yaml: alerts
- deploy/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/gateway_streaming_tools_triage.json: dashboard
- docs/internal/runbooks/streaming_tools_telemetry.md: how to use metrics during support escalations

Verification
- Load test on staging using redwood-examples streaming + tool-call scenarios (forced disconnect + partial args) shows expected reason attribution.
- Confirmed label cardinality stays bounded under route normalization.
- Confirmed alerts are gated by minimum traffic so they don’t flap in low-volume environments.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Consider adding a sampled log line (rate-limited) for unknown disconnects to help refine taxonomy.
- DevEx docs refresh will link to the dashboard and call out common disconnect reasons (tracked in ENG-2850).

Review conversation (highlights)
- Amara Diallo: “Can we avoid model labels? We’ve been burned by cardinality.”
  - Allison Grant: “Agree; no model label. Route is normalized (no IDs), tier is coarse. Added unit test to assert label set.”
- Brian Murphy: “Is ‘proxy_error’ too broad? We might want idle_timeout vs reset.”
  - Allison Grant: “Split out idle_timeout explicitly; proxy_error is only for reset/broken pipe/EOF from downstream. Added comments + mapping table.”
- Ibrahim Khan: “Please ensure metrics line up with the event semantics we’re documenting for tool deltas.”
  - Allison Grant: “Tool counters are stage-based (delta vs final) and don’t assume SDK semantics beyond ‘args incomplete at end-of-stream’. Added note in runbook to match SDK guidance.”
- Owen Phillips: “Alert thresholds: can we exclude client_cancel so on-call isn’t paged for normal cancels?”
  - Allison Grant: “Done; alerts filter out client_cancel and require min traffic.”

CI
- build (linux/amd64): pass
- unit tests: pass
- lint/staticcheck: pass
- integration (gateway smoke): pass

Merge
- Squash merged into main.

Refs
- Linear: ENG-2850 (troubleshooting docs), ENG-2848 (tool-call delta semantics)
- Support: SUP-18421 (disconnects), SUP-18455 (tool parse errors)
- Related: PR 18321 (gateway validation + docs alignment for tool call streaming events)
